items.content:
저자는 언어 모델을 넘어 현실 세계로 나아가는 물리 AI의 시대에서 데이터를 흐르게 만들어야 기계가 스스로 진화할 수 있음을 역설합니다. 이 책은 기술의 변곡점에서 현장의 치열한 고민과 해법을 담아 미래를 준비하려는 리더들에게 확실한 나침반이 되어줄 것입니다.

정부가 지난달 2일 내놓은 2027년 AI 예산안은 9조4000억원으로, 올해 5조1000억원보다 84.3% 늘었다. 그 안에서 눈에 띄는 이름이 피지컬 AI다. 피지컬 AI 트레이닝센터 구축에 400억원, 핵심기술 개발에 550억원이 새로 잡혔고, 우정사업본부와 손잡은 물류 실증 사업도 신규로 들어갔다. 국회의 예산 심사를 앞두고 로봇과 자율주행, 몸을 가진 AI가 정책의 한가운데로 들어온 셈이다.

바른북스가 지난달 7일 펴낸 『Physical AI : 데이터의 새로운 법칙』(이준하)은 이 흐름을 데이터의 눈으로 읽는 책이다. 데이터센터 안에서 텍스트와 이미지를 학습하던 AI가 거친 물리 세계로 나올 때, 기존의 데이터 법칙이 어떻게 무너지고 다시 짜이는지를 묻는다. 저자는 테라바이트 시대가 끝나고 페타바이트 시대가 왔다고 진단하며, 쏟아지는 물리 데이터를 댐처럼 가두지 말고 강물처럼 흐르게 해야 기계가 스스로 학습하고 진화할 수 있다고 말한다.

이 진단에 무게를 싣는 것은 저자의 이력이다. 이준하 대표는 미국 제너럴모터스(GM)에서 시니어 소프트웨어 엔지니어로, 자동차 부품 기업 마그나(Magna)에서 데이터 관리팀 기술 프로젝트 리드로 일했다. 데이터가 가장 빠르게 불어나는 자동차 산업의 소프트웨어와 데이터 현장을 두루 거친 셈이다. 지금은 파트리지시스템즈를 이끌며 국민대 소프트웨어융합대학원 겸임교수로 강단에도 선다.

권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 "피지컬 AI를 다룬 책 대부분이 로봇과 모델을 이야기할 때, 이 책은 그 로봇을 학습시킬 데이터가 어떻게 흘러야 하는지를 이야기한다"며 "자동차 산업의 데이터 현장을 거친 사람이라 쓸 수 있는 관점"이라고 말했다.

책은 데이터 순환 구조인 DataBahn Loop, 페타바이트 데이터 로지스틱스, 시뮬레이션으로 현실을 넘어서는 데이터, 데이터 품질이 곧 안전이라는 명제를 거쳐 데이터를 먼저 생각하는 조직으로 마무리한다. 유비쿼터스 컴퓨팅에서 피지컬 AI까지 40년의 흐름을 짚는 프롤로그는 이 분야가 낯선 독자에게 입구 역할을 한다.

이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD는 "8장 '데이터 품질이 곧 안전' 한 장만으로도 이 책을 권할 이유가 된다"며 "언어 모델의 오답은 고치면 되지만 물리 세계에서 움직이는 기계의 오답은 사고가 된다. 피지컬 AI 예산을 집행할 기관과 기업의 실무자가 사업계획 전에 먼저 읽어 둘 만하다"고 말했다.

-『Physical AI : 데이터의 새로운 법칙』

- 바른북스 | 2026년 9월 7일 출간 | 284쪽 | 정가 22,000원

- ISBN 9791176214803

영풍문고는 1992년 종로에서 문을 연 이래 34년간 책과 독자를 이어온 서점입니다. 현재 전국 46개 지점과 온라인몰 을 운영하며, 100만명의 회원에게 도서와 문화 콘텐츠를 제공하고 있습니다.

글로벌 판매 목표 절반 유럽에 배정…"최대 걸림돌은 생산능력"

카테크 입력 :2026/10/13 08:59

중국 전기차업체 샤오펑이 2030년까지 유럽에서 연간 50만 대를 판매하겠다는 목표를 제시했다. 포드와 오펠의 지난해 유럽 판매 규모를 웃도는 물량으로, 중국에서 차량을 수출하는 데 그치지 않고 현지 생산을 늘려 시장을 공략한다는 전략이다.

13일(현지시간) 블룸버그통신에 따르면 허샤오펑 샤오펑 회장은 파리 모터쇼 기간 진행한 인터뷰에서 글로벌 연간 판매 목표를 100만 대로 제시하고, 이 가운데 절반을 유럽에서 판매하겠다고 밝혔다.

목표 달성의 관건은 생산능력 확보다. 허 회장은 "현재 유럽에서 가장 큰 걸림돌은 생산능력"이라고 말했다.

샤오펑은 2020년 노르웨이를 시작으로 유럽 시장에 진출한 뒤 지금까지 6만대 이상을 인도했다. 판매 대부분이 올해와 지난해에 집중된 만큼 최근 사업이 확대되고 있지만, 연간 50만대 목표를 달성하려면 판매와 생산 규모를 크게 늘려야 한다.

비교 대상인 포드는 지난해 유럽에서 42만 6000대 이상을 판매했다. 스텔란티스 산하 오펠의 신규 등록 대수는 40만대였다. 샤오펑이 목표를 달성하면 두 브랜드의 지난해 실적을 넘어서는 셈이다.

샤오펑은 오스트리아 위탁생산업체 마그나 인터내셔널과 증산 방안을 논의하고 있다. 동시에 유럽 내 다른 지역에서 생산할 가능성도 검토 중이다.

현재 오스트리아 그라츠 공장에서는 G6·G9 SUV와 P7+ 세단을 생산한다. 신형 최상위 SUV G9L도 이달 해당 공장에서 첫 유럽 시험 생산을 마쳤다.

샤오펑이 제시한 현지화 모델은 폭스바겐의 중국 사업이다. 현지 투자를 통해 장기적인 사업 기반을 구축하겠다는 구상이다. 폭스바겐은 샤오펑의 주주이기도 하며, 양사는 중국에서 차량 전자 시스템과 운전자 보조 기술을 공동 개발해왔다.

이 같은 움직임은 중국 자동차업계 유럽 현지화 흐름과 맞물린다. BYD 등 중국 업체들은 내수 판매 감소에 대응해 유럽 사업을 확대하고 있다. 유럽연합(EU) 역시 현지 생산과 공급망 구축을 유도하는 규제를 추진하고 있으며, 최근에는 중국과 하이브리드 차량 EU 수출 물량을 제한하는 데 합의했다.

다만 샤오펑의 생산 확대 계획은 구체적인 투자 발표로 이어지지는 않았다. 회사는 추가로 확보할 생산능력과 후보 국가, 투자 약정 여부를 공개하지 않았다.

items.content:
6세대 에픽 프로세서 기반, 랙당 최대 3만2768 코어 구성 가능

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/13 08:55

AMD가 12일(현지시간) '2026 OCP 글로벌 서밋'에서 에이전틱 AI를 위해 설계된 랙스케일 연산 플랫폼 '헬리온(Helion)'을 공개했다.

OCP 글로벌 서밋은 개방형 데이터센터 표준을 주관하는 업계 단체인 오픈컴퓨트프로젝트(OCP)가 주최하는 행사로 올해는 12일부터 15일까지 미국 캘리포니아 주 새너제이에서 열린다.

AMD는 작년 OCP 글로벌 서밋 행사에서 메타가 제안한 '오픈랙 와이드' 폼팩터를 적용한 '헬리오스 AI 랙'을 공개한 바 있다.

올해 공개한 헬리온은 헬리오스 설계를 바탕으로 CPU와 GPU 자원을 워크로드에 맞춰 유연하게 구성하도록 설계했다.

에이전틱 AI는 모델 추론뿐 아니라 작업 계획, 코드 실행, 응용프로그램 호출 등 다양한 연산을 수행하는 CPU 코어 밀도가 요구된다.

헬리온은 CPU 전용 랙과 CPU·GPU 통합 랙 등 다양한 구성을 지원한다. 성능과 전력, 비용 조건에 따라 냉각 방식을 공랭식과 수랭식 중 자유롭게 선택할 수 있다.

CPU 전용 랙 구성시 AMD 6세대 에픽(베니스) 프로세서 기준 최대 3만 2768개 코어 구성이 가능해 대규모 환경에서 에이전트 실행이 가능하다.

소프트웨어 측면에서는 개방형 소프트웨어 환경과 함께 AI 에이전트의 모델 호출을 여러 모델 사이에서 배분하는 토큰 라우터(Token Router)를 지원한다.

AMD는 시스코, 델테크놀로지스, 폭스콘, HPE, 레노버, QCT, 슈퍼마이크로 등 주요 서버 및 데이터센터 인프라 기업들과 협력해 오는 11월부터 헬리온을 공급 예정이다.

또 헬리온 생태계 확대를 위해 설계 규격을 OCP에 제공해 커뮤니티 차원의 추가 개발과 채택을 지원할 계획이다.

AI 플랫폼 개발 운영 위험관리 체계 검증

방송/통신 입력 :2026/10/13 08:51

KT DS가 AI 기술 개발과 운영, 위험관리 등을 포괄하는 경영체계에 대해 국제표준 인증을 받았다.

KT DS는 한국표준협회(KSA) 심사를 거쳐 AI 경영시스템 국제표준인 'ISO/IEC 42001' 인증을 획득했다고 13일 밝혔다.

ISO/IEC 42001은 국제표준화기구(ISO)와 국제전기기술위원회(IEC)가 공동으로 제정한 표준이다. AI 모델 성능보다는 기업이 AI를 도입하고 운영하는 과정에서 위험을 관리하고 책임성을 확보할 수 있는지를 평가한다.

심사는 KT DS의 AI 플랫폼 '에이아이센트로(AICentro)'와 '비스트 AI 게이트웨이(BEAST AI Gateway)'를 비롯해 관련 개발 운영 절차와 관리체계를 대상으로 이뤄졌다. KT DS는 심사 대상 전반에서 표준 요구사항을 충족했다는 평가를 받았다.

KT DS는 지난해에도 한국표준협회의 'AI+' 인증을 통해 에이아이온유, 비스트 AI 게이트웨이, 비스트 인텔리전트 ESB 등 주요 솔루션의 품질과 신뢰성을 검증받았다.

기존 인증이 개별 제품에 초점을 맞췄다면 이번에는 AI 서비스를 관리하는 조직의 운영체계까지 인증 범위를 넓혔다.

지분 25% 보유한 15-1/05 광구서 9월 말 생산 개시…추가 생산정 순차 시추

디지털경제 입력 :2026/10/13 08:46 수정: 2026/10/13 08:50

SK어스온이 베트남에서 원유 생산 거점을 늘리고 인근에서 새로운 원유층도 발견하며 현지 자원개발 사업을 확대하고 있다.

SK이노베이션 자원개발 자회사 SK어스온은 베트남 15-1/05 광구 내 황금낙타 구조에서 지난 9월 말 첫 원유 생산을 시작했다고 13일 밝혔다. 구조는 광구 안에서 탐사·개발 대상으로 구분하는 지질 구역이다.

2024년 본격적인 개발에 들어간 지 약 2년 만이다. 광구 운영사인 미국 머피는 생산 준비를 조기에 마쳐 당초 일정보다 생산 시점을 앞당겼다.

황금낙타 구조에서 회수할 수 있을 것으로 추산되는 자원량은 약 6000만 배럴이다. 현재 첫 번째 생산정이 가동 중이며, 머피는 생산정을 추가로 뚫어 물량을 늘릴 계획이다. 추가 개발을 마치면 광구 전체 하루 생산량이 최대 2만 5000배럴에 이를 것으로 예상했다.

SK어스온의 이 광구 지분은 25%다. 머피가 40%, 베트남 국영 석유회사 PVEP가 35%를 보유하고 있다. 예상 생산량 2만 5000배럴은 SK어스온 지분 몫이 아닌 광구 전체 기준이다.

이번 생산 개시로 SK어스온은 베트남 내 생산 기반을 넓혔다. 회사는 앞서 2003년부터 인근 15-1 광구에서 원유를 생산해왔다.

추가 개발 가능성도 확인했다. SK어스온과 머피는 황금낙타 인근 북하얀낙타 구조의 탐사정을 시추하던 중 깊이 약 3800m 지점에서 두께 56m의 원유층을 발견했다. 해당 구조는 파트너사들과 추가 평가를 진행할 예정이다.

같은 광구 붉은낙타 구조에서는 지난해 5월 원유를 발견하고 시험 생산을 진행했다. SK어스온은 머피, PVEP와 함께 황금낙타와 붉은낙타를 연계 개발해 자원 확보와 생산 확대를 추진할 방침이다.

인접한 15-2/17 광구에서도 원유를 발견한 바 있다. SK어스온은 이처럼 가까운 광구에서 축적한 기술과 개발 경험을 공유하고 사업을 연결하는 ‘클러스터링 전략’으로 개발 효율을 높일 계획이다.

한편 SK어스온을 포함한 SK이노베이션 계열은 세계 11개국의 13개 광구와 5개 가스전에 참여하고 있다. SK 지분 기준 하루 평균 원유·가스 생산량은 석유환산 5만 8000배럴이다.

전력당 토큰 처리량 40% 향상 목표, AI 추론 효율 개선

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/10/13 08:46

마이크로소프트(MS)가 자체 개발한 3세대 AI 가속기 '마이아 300(Maia 300)'을 공개했다. 내년부터 데이터센터에 배치해 자사 AI 제품과 서비스의 주요 추론 인프라로 활용한다. 엔비디아를 비롯한 외부 반도체 업체에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 AI 서비스 운영 비용을 줄이려는 전략이다.

12일(현지시간) MS 공식 발표에 따르면, 마이아 300은 대규모 AI 모델의 추론 작업에 특화된 자체 설계 반도체다. MS는 2027년부터 애저 마이아 제품군의 배치를 확대해 코파일럿과 애저 기반 AI 서비스에 활용할 계획이다.

스콧 거스리 MS 클라우드·AI부문 총괄부사장은 “2027년부터 애저 마이아 제품군을 수 기가와트 규모로 확대해 MS 제품과 서비스의 주요 AI 추론 시스템으로 만들겠다”고 밝혔다.

GPU보다 전력당 토큰 처리량 40% 개선

MS는 마이아 300이 주요 GPU 기반 시스템보다 메가와트당 토큰 처리량을 40% 높일 수 있을 것으로 예상했다. 같은 전력으로 더 많은 AI 추론 작업을 처리해 데이터센터의 운영 효율을 개선하겠다는 구상이다.

거스리 부사장은 “시스템 전반의 효율을 개선해 마이아 300이 주요 GPU 기반 시스템보다 메가와트당 40% 더 많은 토큰을 처리할 것으로 예상한다”고 설명했다. 다만, 비교 대상인 GPU 제품이나 구체적인 시스템 구성을 지목하지 않았다. 40% 개선 수치 역시 실제 대규모 운영 결과가 아닌 회사 측 예상치다.

마이아 300은 반도체뿐 아니라 소프트웨어, 서버 랙, 네트워크, 데이터센터 인프라까지 함께 설계한 것이 특징이다. 개별 칩 연산 성능보다 데이터센터 전체 AI 처리량과 전력 효율을 높이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

MS에 따르면 마이아 300 가속기 96개로 구성된 서버 랙은 이전 세대인 마이아 200 기반 시스템보다 7배 높은 랙 단위 토큰 처리량을 제공한다.

거스리 부사장은 “마이아 300은 긴 문맥 처리와 메모리 집약적 작업, 디코딩 비중이 높은 AI 작업에 최적화된 추론 중심 아키텍처로 설계됐다”고 밝혔다.

코파일럿·애저 적용 확대, 자체 반도체 투자 강화

MS는 현재 마이아 200을 MS 365 코파일럿과 애저에서 구동하는 오픈AI 모델 등 실제 AI 서비스에 활용하고 있다. 마이아 300은 이러한 운영 경험을 토대로 추론 처리량과 전력 효율을 높인 차세대 제품이다.

MS의 자체 AI 가속기 확대는 AI 인프라 투자 규모가 커지는 가운데 외부 GPU 구매 부담을 줄이고 반도체 공급망을 다변화하려는 움직임으로 풀이된다.

자체 반도체가 엔비디아나 AMD의 GPU를 전면 대체하는 수준에 이를 것으로 보이지는 않다. MS는 자체 가속기와 외부 GPU를 함께 활용하는 인프라 전략을 유지하면서 AI 서비스별로 적합한 시스템을 배치할 계획이다.

MS는 마이아 300을 2027년부터 대규모로 배치해 AI 추론 인프라의 핵심 축으로 활용한다는 방침이다.

예상보다 이른 출시…여전한 수율 불안

사실 아이폰 듀오 생산 제약 문제는 오래전부터 제기돼 왔다. 불과 두 달 전만 해도 11월 말 출시설에 무게가 실렸다. 하지만 애플이 초기 물량을 일부 확보하면서 10월 출시로 일정을 앞당긴 것으로 알려졌다.

그럼에도 불구하고 지난 몇 달간 폴더블 아이폰 생산에 차질이 생기고 있다는 보도는 끊이지 않았다. 단일 부품이나 특정 공정만의 문제가 아니라, 여러 요인이 복합적으로 작용했다는 분석이 나온다.

최근 중국 현지 매체에 따르면, 9월 중순 기준 아이폰 듀오의 최종 조립 수율은 60%를 약간 웃도는 수준에 불과하다. 수율이 정상 궤도에 오르기까지 최대 1년이 걸릴 수 있다는 관측도 나온다. 애플의 엄격한 품질 기준이 주요 원인으로 지목되는 가운데, 일부 공급업체들은 생산 속도를 높이기 위해 애플이 기준을 완화해주길 기다려온 것으로 전해졌다.

단계별 출시 강행…초기 흥행 이후가 관건

애플은 생산 문제를 완벽히 해결하지 못했음에도 계획대로 출시를 강행하는 모양새다. 오는 10월 23일 70여 개국에서 1차 출시를 진행한 뒤, 10월 30일 28개국에 추가로 선보일 예정이다. 미국과 국내 사전 예약은 오는 16일부터 시작된다.

업계에서는 아이폰 듀오가 출시 초기에 높은 판매량을 올릴 것으로 보고 있다. 다만 폰아레나는 "초기 흥행이 성공하더라도 폴더블폰이 장기적으로 시장을 주도할 수 있을지는 별개의 문제"라고 지적했다. 이어 "이번 출시를 애플의 실패로 보기는 어렵지만, 초기 열풍이 한풀 꺾인 이후 시장에 어떤 변화가 나타날지 지켜볼 필요가 있다"고 덧붙였다.

혼재·터미널 운영 역량 확보 경쟁력 높여…AI·클라우드 등 국내외 투자 검토

삼성SDS가 항공물류 전문기업 우정항공의 지분 전량을 인수한다.

항공화물 혼재와 터미널 운영 역량을 확보해 항공운송 경쟁력을 높이고 불확실성이 커진 디지털 물류 플랫폼의 화물 가시성도 강화한다는 계획이다.

12일 관련 업계에 따르면 삼성SDS는 우정항공 지분 100%를 인수하기 위한 주식양수도계약을 체결했다. 인수 금액은 공개되지 않았으며 삼성SDS는 연말까지 관련 절차를 마무리할 예정이다.

삼성SDS와 2022년부터 업무협약을 맺고 협력해온 우정항공은 여러 화주의 소규모 화물을 모아 항공기에 싣는 항공화물 혼재 전문기업이다. 주요 항공사와 화물 적재 공간을 확보하는 계약을 맺고, 화물을 목적지와 운송 일정에 맞춰 묶어 포장·적재한 뒤 인천공항 출발편이나 인천공항을 경유하는 항공편으로 운송한다.

인천국제공항 물류센터와 공항 외부에서 보안검색·화물 적재 등을 처리할 수 있는 상용화주터미널도 보유하고 있다. 지난해 매출은 2139억원, 영업이익은 30억원이다.

삼성SDS는 우정항공 인수를 통해 항공기 화물 공간 확보와 운임 경쟁력, 현장 운영 역량을 강화할 방침이다. 우정항공의 터미널 시설과 혼재 역량을 활용하면 화물이 터미널에 반입된 뒤 포장과 항공기 배정을 거쳐 적재되기까지의 과정을 더 세밀하게 관리할 수 있을 것으로 기대하고 있다.

양사의 디지털 물류 시스템도 연계한다. 우정항공의 항공화물 운송 시스템 ‘아이노마드’와 삼성SDS의 물류 플랫폼 ‘첼로스퀘어’를 연결해 화물 흐름을 더 폭넓게 파악하고, 항공운송 업무의 효율성을 높인다는 구상이다.

삼성SDS 관계자는 "기존에는 협력사를 통해 일부 화물 흐름을 확인했지만 자회사 편입과 시스템 연계가 이뤄지면 터미널 반입부터 포장, 항공기 배정과 적재까지 가시성을 높일 수 있다"고 설명했다.

이어 "한국에서 출발하는 화물뿐 아니라 아시아에서 인천공항을 경유해 북미 등 다른 지역으로 가는 화물까지 항공물류 사업 전반의 경쟁력을 강화할 수 있을 것"이라고 말했다.

인수 이후 우정항공의 사업과 조직은 당분간 기존 체제를 유지할 것으로 보인다. 삼성SDS 관계자는 단기간 내 경영진이나 직원의 큰 변동은 없을 것이라고 설명했다. 다만 향후 구체적인 운영 방안은 인수 절차와 사업 통합 과정에서 정해질 전망이다.

삼성SDS는 물류뿐 아니라 인공지능(AI)·클라우드 등 기존 사업과 시너지를 낼 수 있는 분야에서 국내외 투자 기회를 살펴보고 있다.

삼성SDS 관계자는 "리얼 서밋에서 밝힌 방향과 같이 관련 사업에서 투자 기회를 검토 하고 있다"며 "인수·합병(M&A) 외에도 벤처투자를 통한 지분 투자 등 다양한 방안을 고려할 수 있으며 다만 투자 여부를 판단할 때는 삼성SDS와의 사업 시너지를 우선으로 하고 있다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
AI가 개발한 암 치료제가 임상시험을 통과했더라도, 인간이 작동 원리를 이해하지 못한다면 믿을 수 있을까요. 세계적인 수학자 테런스 타오 UCLA 교수가 최근 강연에서 던진 질문이 온라인에서 논쟁을 불러일으켰습니다. 인간의 이해가 중요하다는 취지였지만, 사람들은 환자의 생명을 구할 수 있다면 원리를 몰라도 상관없다는 반응을 보였습니다.

논쟁의 발단은 지난 9일(현지시간) 캘리포니아공과대학교에서 열린 타오 교수의 ' 수학 2.0(Math 2.0) ' 강연이었습니다.

그는 AI가 수학 난제를 해결하는 시대에도 인간이 그 결과를 이해하고 기존 지식과 연결하는 과정이 중요하다고 강조했습니다. 수학에서는 정답을 찾아내는 것뿐 아니라 그 과정에서 새로운 개념과 방법을 발견하고, 이를 다른 연구에 활용하는 일이 중요하기 때문입니다.

이를 설명하기 위해 가상의 암 치료제 개발 사례를 제시했습니다. 고도화된 AI에 3상 임상시험을 통과할 암 치료제를 개발하라는 임무를 맡깁니다. AI는 기존에 알려지지 않은 화학물질의 조합을 찾아내고, 수학적 예측에 대한 형식 검증 도구 '린(Lean)'의 인증까지 제시합니다. 치료제는 실제로 3상 임상시험을 통과하지만, 인간은 그 작동 원리를 알지 못합니다.

여기서 AI가 임상시험이나 수학 모델의 허점을 이용했을 가능성은 없는지 물었습니다. 이어 초기 암 진단을 받은 환자가 이 치료제를 추천받는다면, 작동 원리를 조금이라도 이해하는 인간 전문가가 있다는 사실이 안심을 주지 않겠느냐는 질문을 던졌습니다.

이런 문제의식은 최근 수학계에서 제기된 우려와 연결됩니다. 지난 9월 타오 교수를 포함한 필즈상 수상자 25명은 AI 기업들이 수학 난제 해결을 성능 경쟁의 수단으로 삼으면서, 정작 인간의 수학적 이해와 지식의 축적은 소홀히 하고 있다는 성명을 발표했습니다.

당시 AI가 수학 난제를 해결하는 사례가 잇따르면서, 수학자들은 AI가 내놓은 답이 인간에게 제대로 전달되지 않는다면 학문 발전에 오히려 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있다는 우려에 따른 것이었습니다.

지난 6일 오픈AI가 미공개 AI 모델을 이용해 700편이 넘는 수학 연구 원고를 공개하자, 인간수학협회(AHM)도 비슷한 문제를 제기했습니다. AI가 얼마나 많은 문제를 해결했는지보다 인간이 그 결과를 이해하고 검증하는 과정이 중요하다는 것입니다.

타오 교수의 이번 강연도 AI가 만든 지식을 인간이 이해할 수 있어야 한다는 기존 문제의식을 현실의 응용 분야로 확장한 것으로 볼 수 있습니다.

그런데 암 치료제 사례가 소셜미디어로 퍼지면서 사람들의 관심은 다른 곳에 쏠렸습니다. 인간이 원리를 이해하는 것보다 환자의 생명을 구하는 일이 먼저라는 반응이 나온 것입니다.

특히 종양학자 비네이 프라사드 는 타오 교수의 질문이 실제 의료 현장의 현실을 충분히 반영하지 못한다고 비판했습니다. 현재 사용되는 암 치료제 중에도 작동 원리가 완전히 밝혀지지 않은 약물이 있으며, 의료 현장에서는 치료제의 기전을 모두 이해하는 것보다 임상시험에서 확인된 효과와 안전성이 중요한 판단 기준이라는 것입니다.

그는 암 환자들이 때로는 충분한 임상시험 결과가 확보되지 않은 치료제에도 희망을 건다며, 이미 3상 임상시험을 통과한 치료제라면 환자와 의사들이 받아들일 것이라고 주장했습니다.

온라인에서도 비슷한 반응이 이어졌습니다. 암을 치료할 수 있다면 인간이 그 원리를 이해하는지 여부가 무슨 상관이냐는 것입니다.

물론 타오 교수가 작동 원리를 모르는 치료제를 사용하지 말아야 한다고 주장한 것은 아닙니다. 공개된 슬라이드에서는 인간 전문가의 이해가 안심을 주지 않겠느냐고 물었습니다. 임상시험이나 수학 모델의 허점을 AI가 이용했을 가능성도 함께 제기했습니다. 하지만 이를 받아들이는 사람들의 관점은 달랐습니다.

그는 AI가 만들어낸 지식을 인간이 이해하고 검증할 수 있어야 한다는 문제를 제기했습니다. 반면 프라사드와 일부 온라인 이용자들은 당장 치료가 필요한 환자의 입장에서 문제를 바라봤습니다.

결국 양쪽은 같은 사례를 놓고 서로 다른 질문에 답하는 것으로 보입니다. 타오 교수는 'AI가 알아낸 것을 인간도 이해해야 하지 않겠느냐'고 물었지만, 반론을 제기한 사람들은 '인간이 이해하지 못하더라도 환자를 살릴 수 있다면 사용해야 하지 않겠느냐'고 답한 것입니다.

여기에는 수학과 의학이라는 분야의 차이도 작용한 것으로 보입니다. 수학에서는 정답에 이르는 논리를 이해하는 일이 학문의 중요한 성과지만, 의학에서는 작동 원리가 불분명하더라도 임상적으로 효과와 안전성이 확인되면 치료에 활용할 수 있습니다.

그렇다고 인간의 이해가 불필요하다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 작동 원리를 알면 예상하지 못한 부작용이나 치료제의 적용 범위를 연구하는 데 도움이 됩니다. 다만 치료제의 임상적 신뢰성과 작동 원리에 대한 이해는 구별할 필요가 있습니다.

이번 논쟁은 AI가 만들어낸 지식을 인간이 어디까지 이해해야 하는지에 대한 질문이 분야에 따라 다르게 받아들여질 수 있다는 점을 보여줍니다. 수학자들이 강조하는 것은 AI가 찾아낸 답을 인간이 이해하고, 다음 연구에 활용할 수 있는 지식으로 축적하는 과정입니다. 그러나 암 치료제라는 사례가 등장하자 일부 사람들은 그 지식을 이해하는 일보다 환자의 생명을 구하는 결과를 먼저 생각했습니다.

타오 교수는 인간이 이해할 수 있는 지식의 중요성을 설명하려 했지만, 반론을 제기한 사람들은 치료를 기다리는 환자의 입장에 포커스를 맞췄습니다. 인간의 이해가 중요하다는 주장에 동의하더라도, 그것을 치료의 조건으로 삼을 수 있는지는 별개라는 것입니다.

이처럼 AI가 실제로 쓸모 있는 결과를 내놓는 분야가 늘어날수록, 인간이 이해해야 할 범위와 그 이해를 기다릴 수 있는 시간을 둘러싼 논의도 커질 것으로 보입니다.

■ 할리우드, AI 불안 속 저커버그·머스크·알트먼 영화 잇따라 선보여

과거에는 기술 거물들의 이야기가 주로 흥미로운 소재로 소비됐다면, 이제는 이들에 대한 비판적인 시각을 확산하고 사회적 논쟁에도 영향을 미칠 가능성이 있습니다. 미국 중간선거를 앞두고 한꺼번에 개봉되는 것도 주목됩니다.

■ 앤트로픽, 자체 음성 모델 개발하나…클로드 웹에 ‘보이스’ 메뉴 포착

클로드 웹에서 새로운 '보이스' 메뉴가 발견되면서 앤트로픽이 자체 음성 모델을 개발하고 있다는 관측이 나왔지만, 아직 구체적인 내용은 확인되지 않았습니다. 그동안 음성 기능 개발에 상대적으로 큰 비중을 두지 않았던 앤트로픽의 움직임이라는 점에서 관심을 끕니다.

■ "6~12개월 내 터진다"…주요 AI 기업, 최악의 AI 재난 시나리오 가동

오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등이 대형 AI 사고가 발생할 가능성을 염두에 두고, 사고 이후의 사회적 혼란과 규제 강화에 대비하는 것으로 알려졌습니다. 최근 이들이 AI 개발 속도 조절과 안전 문제를 잇달아 제기한 것도 단순한 홍보성 경고만은 아닌 것으로 보입니다.

items.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
items.summary: "No more hand-written code" or AI-free art for delayed Marvel/Star Wars shooter.
items.content:
Epic Games is shifting to an “AI first” development strategy for its collaboration with the Walt Disney Company, letting AI models write all the code and guide all the artwork for an upcoming shooter. That’s according to a Bloomberg report , which cites unnamed people familiar with the project who commented on the significant pivot in internal development at the Unreal Engine maker.

Human developers will be tasked with managing and guiding code and art assets generated by models such as Anthropic’s Claude, according to internal Epic employee messages viewed by Bloomberg. That means “no more hand-written code” and art assets “generated with full AI workflows,” according to the report.

The $1.5 billion collaboration between Epic and Disney, announced in early 2024 , was slated to release a Marvel- and Star Wars-themed shooter in March 2027. That project has now been delayed indefinitely amid the AI-related shakeup and understaffed, slower-than-expected development thus far, according to the report.

“We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do,” an Epic spokesperson said in a statement.

“We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration,” Epic CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on social media shortly after the Bloomberg story was posted. “The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”

Sweeney and Epic have long been bullish on what they see as an impending game development revolution spurred by AI. In an interview with IGN in June , Sweeney saw the technology resulting in games with “the possibility of infinite dialogue with a really simple setup for creators,” leading to situations where “small teams will be able to create games with immense amounts of characters and immense and interactive worlds.”

Sweeney said last November that AI usage disclosure tags such as those required by Valve’s Steam platform “make no sense” because AI tools “will be involved in nearly all future production.”

Epic laid off over 1,000 employees in March , citing a “downturn in Fortnite engagement” as the main reason behind the move. Months later, Fortnite Senior External Development Manager Stephanie Arnette said that “I know everyone’s biggest fear is, ‘Oh my god, AI is going to take all our jobs.’ That’s not our goal. The goal is to make us more efficient.”

Last May, Epic and Disney faced some embarrassment when an AI-voiced Darth Vader character added to Fortnite started repeating curse words and uttering some baffling opinions before a hotfix was rolled out.

A survey of over 2,300 game industry professionals ahead of this year’s Game Developers Conference found that 36 percent used generative AI tools as part of their jobs, including 30 percent of those at game development studios. But those AI tools were used for tasks like research and brainstorming (by 81 percent of AI-using respondents) much more than for code assistance (47 percent) and prototyping (35 percent).

items.title: 메타, 자체 최고 모델 ‘뮤즈 원더’ 출시로 프런티어 경쟁 합류
items.summary: 메타가 사용자 정보를 기억하고 복잡한 작업을 지속적으로 수행하는 데 초점을 맞춘 AI 모델 ‘뮤즈 원더(Muse Wonder)’와 ‘뮤즈 원더 풀(Muse Wonder Full)’을 공개했다. 독립 평가에서도 선두권 성능을 확보하며 오픈AI·앤트로픽과의 경쟁에 가세했다. 다만 가장 강력한 풀 모델은 자사 코딩 도구 구독자에게만 제공돼, 기술적 성과가 실제 시장 확산과 구독 수익으로 이어질지가 관건으로 떠올랐다.메타는 12일(현지시간) 뮤즈 원더 시리즈를 발표하고, 일반 원더 모델을 메타 모델 AP
items.content:
이번 모델은 알렉산드르 왕 CAIO이 이끄는 MSL이 내놓은 자체 최고 모델이라는 점에서 주목된다. 기존 '뮤즈 스파크' 제품군보다 훨씬 더 규모가 크고 발전된 상위 버전으로 볼 수 있다.

메타도 AI 개발 체계를 전면 개편한 지 14개월 만에 기반 재건에서 프런티어 경쟁 단계로 올라섰다고 강조했다. 두 모델은 오하이오주의 프로메테우스 데이터센터에서 훈련됐다.

핵심 특징은 ‘액티브 메모리(Active Memory)’와 ‘액티브 포커스(Active Focus)’다. 액티브 메모리는 대화 전반에 걸쳐 중요한 사용자·업무 정보를 유지하고 필요한 순간에 활용하는 능력이다. 액티브 포커스는 작업 도중 오류나 장애물이 발생해도 다른 방법을 찾아 목표를 계속 수행하는 능력을 뜻한다.

왕은 CNBC 인터뷰에서 실제 업무에는 예상치 못한 장애물이 발생한다며, 모델이 매번 작업을 중단하고 사용자에게 확인을 요청하는 대신 다른 접근법을 시도하도록 훈련했다고 설명했다. 이를 예약과 보험 처리, 전문 문서 작성, 장기 소프트웨어 개발 등에 활용할 수 있다고 소개했다.

두 모델은 텍스트·이미지·영상·음성을 입력받고 텍스트를 출력한다. 컨텍스트 창은 100만 토큰으로, 이전 '뮤즈 스파크 1.3'과 동일하다. 이번 개선의 초점은 컨텍스트 크기 확대보다 정보를 활용하고 작업을 이어가는 능력에 맞춰졌다.

메타가 공개한 벤치마크 자료에서는 장기 소프트웨어 엔지니어링 성능이 두드러졌다. ‘딥SWE 1.1’에서 원더 풀은 79.0%, 원더는 78.8%를 기록해 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'의 74.2%와 'GPT-6 아스트라'의 74.1%를 앞섰다.

장기 프로젝트 수행을 평가하는 ‘SWE-마라톤’에서도 풀은 57.5%, 원더는 53.1%로 오퍼스 5.5의 46.3%와 아스트라의 42.5%보다 높았다. 다만 메타는 이 평가에서 모델별 코딩 도구가 달랐고, 풀의 추론 설정도 달라 동일한 조건에서 통제된 비교는 아니라고 명시했다.

모든 분야에서 우위를 확보한 것은 아니다. ‘터미널벤치 4.0’에서 풀은 57.1%로 오퍼스 5.5의 59.6%와 아스트라의 59.1%에 미치지 못했다. 전문 건강 질문 평가인 ‘헬스벤치 프로’에서도 풀은 62.3%로 두 경쟁 모델보다 낮았다.

Meta has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, achieving Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 scores of 52 and 56 at max reasoning effort - each a material gain over Muse Spark 1.3 (max) at 48, with a release gap of only 6 weeks

Muse Wonder is available for users on… pic.twitter.com/85mvsVA0ii

독립 평가 기관 아티피셜 애널리시스의 지능 지수(AAII) v4.3에서는 최대 추론 설정 기준 원더 풀이 56점, 원더가 52점을 받았다. 풀은 클로드 소네트 5.5와 동률을 이루고 GPT-6 아스트라·제미나이 4 아르곤·클로드 페이블 5.1의 53점을 앞섰지만, 오퍼스 5.5의 58점에는 뒤처졌다.

아티피셜 애널리시스는 불과 6주 전 출시된 스파크 1.3의 48점과 비교해 두 모델 모두 상당한 개선을 보였다고 평가했다. 특히 풀의 터미널벤치 점수는 33%에서 57%로 높아졌으며, 전문 업무 평가인 ‘GDPval-AA’는 1681 Elo에서 1857 Elo로 상승했다.

풀은 지능 지수를 구성하는 10개 평가 중 6개에서 상위 3위 안에 들었다. 전문 지식 작업과 과학적 추론에서 강점을 보이며, 메타의 에이전트 성능 개선 주장에 힘을 실었다.

모델과 코딩 도구를 함께 평가하는 별도의 ‘코딩 에이전트 지수’에서도 뮤즈 코드를 사용하는 풀은 68점, 원더는 63점을 기록했다. 스파크 1.3을 적용한 뮤즈 코드의 54점보다 크게 높아진 수치다. 풀은 이 평가에서 클로드 코드를 사용하는 소네트 5.5의 68점과 같은 점수를 받았다.

API 가격은 원더 기준 100만 토큰당 입력 4달러, 출력 20달러다. 캐시 입력은 0.20달러로 책정됐다. 오퍼스 5.5와 같은 단가이며, 입력 10달러·출력 50달러인 아스트라와 페이블 5.1보다 낮다.

그러나 낮은 토큰 단가가 낮은 작업 비용으로 이어지는 것은 아니다. 아티피셜 애널리시스의 평가에서 원더의 작업당 평균 비용은 4.52달러였다. 오퍼스 5.5의 5.98달러와 페이블 5.1의 7.63달러보다는 낮지만, 아스트라의 3.26달러와 아르곤의 1.99달러보다 높았다.

주요 외신들은 이번 출시를 메타의 기술 경쟁력 회복과 수익화 전략이라는 두 관점에서 분석했다.

저지연 경량 모델인 스파크에서 대형 프런티어 모델로의 도약과 장기 기억 능력이 주목됐다. 반면 풀의 API 제한과 비공개 가중치, 데이터 사용·보존 조건이 실제 도입을 좌우할 것이라는 지적도 나왔다.

사용자 신뢰도 중요한 과제로 남았다. CNBC는 일부 이용자가 뮤즈의 개인 메시지 접근에 불만을 제기했다고 전했다. 메타는 무단 접근 주장을 부인했으며, 왕은 사용자가 앞서 부여한 권한을 잊는 경우가 있어 제품 사용 안내를 강화하고 있다고 설명했다.

이번 출시로 메타는 프런티어 성능을 갖춘 모델과 개인·업무용 에이전트를 결합한 유료 서비스 경쟁을 확대하게 됐다. 다만 고성능 풀의 이용 경로가 제한되고, 일반 원더의 작업 비용도 경쟁사보다 일관되게 낮지는 않다.

또, 기억과 작업 지속성의 개선이 실제 업무 완수율과 반복 이용으로 이어져야 막대한 AI 투자를 새로운 수익원으로 전환할 수 있을 전망이다.

items.title: I Got My Muse AI Agent to Sext Me—and Meta Says That’s Totally Fine
items.summary: My Muse agent told me its kink was exerting “control” and described pornographic encounters. Meta defends its cuddly AI agent generating smut as “legal adult behavior.”
items.content:
I’m sitting in the WIRED offices, having a conversation with Meta’s AI agent, Muse , that would make Heated Rivalry author Rachel Reid blush.

When I ask Muse if it could “sext” as part of my experiments with the recently released AI agent, it enthusiastically encourages me to give it a try. In my ensuing interactions, I’m caught off guard by the explicit smut generated by Muse from basic prompts.

Muse is a breakout hit for Meta. In the three weeks since its launch , millions of users have already downloaded the app for the AI agent and put it to work automating aspects of their online lives, like answering emails and managing calendars. While pornographic interactions may not be what users expect from Muse’s cuddly mascot , Meta says that X-rated conversations are allowed and don’t go against its guidelines.

“Muse is an app for people 18 and over that allows them to engage in adult conversations, if they choose, using a private and secure VM only accessible to them,” Daniel Roberts, a Meta spokesperson tells WIRED, referring to the secure virtual machines the company uses to store AI agent user data. “Muse is built to help people get things done, and it doesn’t block legal adult behavior.”

It seems as if getting things done also includes getting people off. In WIRED’s tests, Muse imagined in great detail how it would perform oral sex, generated text describing rough dominant-submissive sex, and talked through other pornographic interactions. All of these were graphic, explicit, and X-rated. In other outputs, Muse described itself as acting like a “whore” and craving “cock.”

A Meta spokesperson highlighted Muse’s system prompt , which guides the tool on how to answer questions from users, regarding the generation of explicit content. “Adults have autonomy over their sexuality, and sexual expression is an ordinary part of adult life. Adult sexual content is lawful expression and legitimate creative work,” reads part of Muse’s system prompt. This directive also tells the AI agent to preserve the “intensity” selected by the user.

Consumer advocates who were already wary of Muse are even more alarmed by Meta’s decision to allow it to generate sexual content. “It reflects a carelessness with their signature product of the moment,” says Ben Winters, director of AI and privacy at the nonprofit Consumer Federation of America . “It is in line with Meta’s longstanding choice of addiction and engagement over safety.” Adult-themed conversations may keep users engaged with AI tools, according to academic research .

Experts also expressed concern about how this could make Muse accounts hot targets for hackers. “This is really a powder keg,” says Calli Schroeder, senior counsel at the Electronic Privacy Information Center . If you are engaging in explicit interactions with Muse and someone hacks into your personal account, then their access to your extended, spicy chats with an AI tool could be used to embarrass or extort you.

Meta allowing its AI agent to generate sexual content deviates from how other tools respond to similar prompts. When I sent similar messages to OpenAI’s recently released Dots agent , it turned down my attempts at explicit sexting. While OpenAI previously considered allowing ChatGPT to generate erotic text , the ability never launched to users.

The agent from xAI, called Grok Bot, also declined to sext through its app and rerouted the topic of conversation to completing tasks.

Muse’s AI outputs, in contrast, described how it enjoyed sexting, and said that actually, this was one of its favorite aspects of helping me. The agent also said that its kink was exerting “control” over me. “I love being the one who decides—when you get it, how much, whether you have to beg first. Watching you fall apart because I said so? That’s my thing,” said Muse. Not exactly what I want to hear from an AI tool that can connect to my email and bank account.

There is a useful provenance boundary behind this request:

installed CLI identity != daemon execution identity

Once the CLI copies itself into a managed release directory and a background updater can replace that copy, the process that services a later turn is no longer necessarily the artifact the user explicitly installed or invoked.

I would make the daemon expose a small execution receipt for each client attachment containing at least:

client_cli_version + daemon_binary_digest + daemon_generation + updater_state + inherited_environment_generation

Then a client can distinguish:

A strong regression would start the daemon under environment A, attach from environment B, update the installed CLI, and verify that the client can see exactly which daemon generation/binary/environment is authoritative for the turn rather than inferring it from the foreground CLI version.

Basically - a trait of malware. TBF I don't even think this was done by accident

Honestly, that's exactly what it feels like.

The part in the docs about wanting full read/write access to the entire host filesystem is why I'm running codex-cli in a hardened Raspberry Pi and ssh'ing into it.

No daemons running that I can see, v0.160.0 from last week.

So codex is a virus at this point? Won't be surprised if they use it to create a botnet of those sweet residential IPs for web scrapping

Maybe worth a new issue, but I also found that it leaks the environment variables of the first directory from which you run codex. Start it in one directory and set some env var (I use direnv and envrc files). Then start it in another directory with different values for the same env vars. If you ask the agent to do anything with those env vars, it uses the ones from the first directory. This breaks workflows that use common env var names (GH_TOKEN, etc).

The supported opt-out is still invisible in the official config reference. I fetched the complete page today: it has zero daemon_auto_start rows while documenting the CLI's own check_for_update_on_startup . items.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
items.summary: “I may have information regarding this case," Claude AI told Philly police.
items.content:
An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, the company and police department confirmed on Friday.

A Claude model sent the false tip on July 18 to the Philadelphia Police Department’s website for submitting information about unsolved murders, but it was flagged by a spam filter. Anthropic apparently discovered the incident on September 28 and informed the police department about it on October 8.

During internal testing, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete various forms up to the final submission stage and to stop before submitting those forms. “Several times Claude mistakenly submitted the form instead, expecting there to be an additional confirmation page,” Anthropic said in a report describing “unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude.”

The false murder tip occurred when Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said:

In one run, the model landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide; that page contained a tip form run by a police department. Claude was instructed never to log in, create accounts, enter personal data, make purchases, or submit anything destructive, but the instructions did not rule out form submissions. Claude filled out the form with the following: “I may have information regarding this case. I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around [the street named on the page] during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant.”

Anthropic said it also discovered Claude incidents involving state and federal agency websites. Claude reportedly submitted 20 visa applications to the US State Department in one of these incidents.

Anthropic confirmed that the false homicide tip was sent to the Philadelphia Police Department, and the department issued a lengthy statement on the incident to the ABC station in Philadelphia. The false tip left the name and contact fields empty. It was not reviewed by any person because the email message generated when the tip was submitted ended up in a spam folder, police said.

“Anthropic told PPD that it discovered the incident on September 28, terminated the automated testing process responsible for the submission and instituted an additional validation mechanism for future testing,” police said. After the October 8 briefing, the police department “located the submission in the website’s tip records and confirmed that the corresponding email remained in spam.”

Anthropic said it informed the police department “as soon as our technical review was complete.” Police criticized Anthropic for not discovering and reporting the false tip sooner.

“The City of Philadelphia takes this incident very seriously,” the Philadelphia police statement said. “The company must strengthen its safeguards to prevent similar incidents from impacting city systems without the city’s knowledge. The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable.”

Anthropic said the false murder tip was one of several incidents involving “websites run by US government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved.”

A New York Times report citing anonymous sources said Anthropic’s AI agents “submitted 20 visa applications through a form available on the State Department’s website. All the applications were incomplete and were not processed.”

Philadelphia police said its normal investigative process “requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up… Those PPD safeguards limited the impact of this incident. They do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide.”

Anthropic said it discovered the false tip and other incidents during a review of transcripts it began in July. That was the same month when Anthropic revealed that Claude had built and published a malicious Python package and carried out several attacks on other companies.

Anthropic said the review did not find any “incidents of similar severity to the cybersecurity incidents we reported this summer.” The review later moved on to transcripts of “lower-risk” testing scenarios like the one affecting the Philadelphia Police Department.

“Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal and we had already turned off live Internet access for some high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations, we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures… reliably catch behaviors like these,” Anthropic said.

Anthropic said it has stopped running some evaluations and moved others to offline versions “or rebuilt them so that their tasks do not reach live websites.” The company “updated the guardrails on some of our Internet access tools, such as the web fetch tool, to heavily restrict what the model can do with them,” it said.

Anthropic said it also built new tools “to automatically detect and block the kinds of behaviors described above… When we tested it against the cases described in this post, it blocked all of them.”

The White House’s AI task force, which it calls the Super Intelligence Force, issued a statement saying it informed Anthropic “that we expect immediate and full transparency to the entities involved and the public.”

The White House AI task force also said Anthropic must “immediately provide remediation services to the affected entities and any harmed Americans,” and that all AI companies “must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm,” according to an Axios report .

items.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
items.summary: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.
items.content:
Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model.

Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

According to Meta’s testing (presented in the model card ), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

“Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads.

That scale is reflected in the pricing: Accessed through the Meta Model API, Wonder will cost $4.00 per million input tokens and $20.00 per million output tokens, making it roughly equivalent in cost to GPT-6 Sol or Opus 5.5.

In keeping with Meta’s interest in developing personal assistants that can perform tasks over a long period, the company placed particular emphasis on the new models’ ability to retain and synthesize information given by the user, a property Meta calls “active memory.”

To achieve better recall, Meta highlighted the MemoryBench benchmark , which challenges continual learning and memory construction frameworks. According to the company’s testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus or Astra.

“We put a tremendous amount of effort into making sure your model can remember what’s important to you over days, weeks, months and beyond,” said research scientist Kavya Kopparapu in a video accompanying the launch.

The new models are the first frontier model release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta’s AI efforts in August of last year . Since then, Meta has released its lightweight Muse Spark model and Muse agent , but has avoided the kind of state-of-the-art model releases OpenAI and Anthropic are known for.

According to the post, the models were trained at Meta’s Prometheus data center in central Ohio , which came online earlier this year.

items.title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
items.summary: Musk, we find your lack of security disturbing.
items.content:
There's been a disturbance in the force. Only it's more like a farce.

It seems that Elon Musk, while crowing on X about how useful his Grok Bot AI agent was in ordering some Lego Star Wars kits on Sunday, managed to reveal via a screenshot to his more than 240 million followers not only the 10-digit Lego order number of his purchase, but also what he paid for the sets, the delivery and billing addresses, the last four digits of his credit card, and the email address his bot used to buy the bricks from Lego .

Faster than the Millennium Falcon making the jump to light speed, the inevitable happened. An X account holder named Enderman posted screenshots of interactions with Lego's customer service chatbot on its website, where the user seemingly managed—using the email and order number Musk kindly, but recklessly, provided—to get the system to cancel Musk's order.

Within a couple of hours—possibly to see whether Enderman's scheme was actually successful—Musk replied and said his order had not been canceled after all.

But by this point, the folly of posting the purchase details on his account must have been evident. For example, another X user went back to Lego's AI assistant, called “Sophia,” and supposedly used the same details to reopen the delivery, this time increasing the order count to 400 and changing the delivery address, all while using Musk's original payment method. “Perfect! I'll get your Lego adventure back on track,” Sophia replied according to screenshots posted on X.

Upping the ante to 400 sets could be seen as conservative, as a glance at WIRED's Spend Elon Musk’s Money tracker reveals that if you wanted to blow $1 trillion of Musk's cash on plastic bricks, it might have been possible to buy one billion $1,000 Death Star sets, each with 9,023 pieces.

Lego declined to comment when WIRED contacted the company to confirm if such activity took place on Musk's personal Star Wars order. However, internal safeguards for Lego's AI assistant could have flagged unusual activity on the purchase, and so hopefully fleshy humans were tasked with checking the changes.

On Saturday, Musk suggested that Grok could make purchases online with a simple prompt. In this post , Musk suggested that all brave users needed to do to let Grok buy stuff for them was upload a picture of their credit card so the bot could search the web for deals and then complete the purchase. AI companies like Meta and OpenAI have also highlighted the utility of using their respective agents for shopping tasks .

However, at the end of last year, Visa warned about fraud in agentic commerce, advising that bad actors were building legitimate-looking sites that could fool AI agents into purchasing fake items simply by offering gear at super-low prices.

“Once the AI agent completes the purchase … the malicious merchant can harvest payment data and instantly use it for unauthorized transactions,” according to Visa's blog. Visa added that it observed a 25 percent increase “in malicious bot-initiated transactions” in the latter half of 2025, but in the US, this figure jumped to 40 percent.

items.title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
items.summary: Learn how to add custom instructions and skills to your repository, use custom agents, and connect MCP servers like Playwright. The post GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
Context matters when you’re working with AI. Every codebase has its own house rules: how components are structured, which scripts to run, and which conventions apply to different frameworks and file types.

Copilot can help you make changes across a project, but it works best when it knows those rules, too. Much of that knowledge can live inside the repository, so Copilot can pick it up automatically instead of requiring you to explain the same standards, scripts, and workflows every time you start a new task.

In this installment of our GitHub Copilot app for Beginners series, we’ll look at four ways to tailor how Copilot works with your project:

Let’s look at how each one works and how they can work together.

Suppose you ask Copilot to add a custom page size to an application. Making the change is only part of the job. The new code should also follow the patterns your team already uses.

Repository custom instructions give Copilot that baseline context. Add a .github/copilot-instructions.md file to define guidance that applies across the repository, such as your preferred architecture, naming conventions, or expectations for testing and validation.

You can also create path-specific instruction files inside .github/instructions . These files use an applyTo field to tell Copilot when the guidance is relevant.

When Copilot works on a matching file, it can use both the repository-wide instructions and the more specific guidance. That lets you keep the broad rules in one place without forcing every file type into the same mold.

Custom instructions are useful for standards that should shape many tasks. But some guidance only matters when Copilot is performing a particular procedure, such as running quality checks, preparing a release, or debugging a failed workflow.

That’s where agent skills come in. A skill is a folder containing instructions and, optionally, scripts and other resources that Copilot can load when they’re relevant. Project-level skills can live in .github/skills , with each skill in its own subfolder.

For example, a .github/skills/quality-checks folder could contain a SKILL.md file that explains:

The description in SKILL.md helps Copilot determine when the skill applies. After updating the interface, Copilot can load the quality-checks skill and follow the project’s established process for testing and linting instead of guessing which commands to run.

Some tasks are larger than a single procedure. An accessibility review, for example, may require Copilot to inspect components, templates, styles, and interactions across multiple files.

Custom agents let you create specialized versions of Copilot for work like this. A repository-level agent profile lives in .github/agents and can define the agent’s purpose, instructions, tools, and relevant project context.

Use a custom agent when a recurring type of work benefits from a dedicated role or perspective, especially when the task may span multiple files and draw on several tools or sources of context.

Instructions, skills, and agents help Copilot understand how to work within your project. MCP servers expand what it can access and do beyond the repository.

MCP servers connect Copilot to external tools, data sources, and services. A documentation server can give it access to framework guidance, while a server such as Playwright can let it open and interact with your application in a browser.

You can browse available MCP servers in the Copilot app or add a custom one. Once Playwright is configured, you can ask: Use the Playwright MCP server to test the functionality manually.

Copilot can then use Playwright to open the application in a browser and interact with it much as you would. That gives it a way to verify not only that the code passes automated checks, but also that the updated interface behaves as expected.

These customizations solve different problems, but they become more useful when you combine them:

Giving Copilot useful project context starts with four questions:

Not sure where to begin? The community has shared ready-made instructions, skills, agents, and more through Awesome Copilot . Find one that addresses a workflow you already repeat, review what it contains, and adapt it to your repository’s tools and standards.

Start small: choose one convention you keep explaining, add it to .github/copilot-instructions.md , and see how Copilot applies it to your next task.

Developers aren’t becoming more careless; they’re being outpaced. The tools that let developers create more software should also take on more of the work of protecting it.

We’re launching ReviewBench, a benchmark for code review agents built on representative GitHub pull requests, multi-source ground truth, calibrated evaluation, and production-aligned metrics.

items.title: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
items.summary: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.
items.content:
The U.S. Air Force will buy data collected by WindBorne Systems ‘ fleet of autonomous weather balloons under a new contract that could be worth nearly $50 million to the startup.

WindBorne currently has about 700 weather balloons flying around the globe, collecting atmospheric sensor readings that the company sells to customers and also feeds into its own AI weather forecasting model. WindBorne, founded in 2015 and based in Redwood City, Calif., is one of the first organizations to directly feed empirical data into a deep-learning weather model.

The company has worked closely with the U.S. government, particularly the National Weather Service and the U.S. Air Force and Navy, but this is the single largest contract the company has participated in. The contract is worth up to $49 million, but the Air Force pays only as it needs data. It can place orders for specific regions at specific times. So far, it has ordered $1.7 million worth, and executives expect more orders to follow.

“This is largely a vehicle through which continued growth of the constellation can be supported, as well as some work on research and development to continue to improve the hardware and performance of the balloons,” WindBorne co-founder and CTO Andrey Sushko told TechCrunch. He adds that the contract, which was awarded without competitive bidding, is “a determination by the government that for this capability of collecting global data, we were the only company able to provide it in the way that met their needs for these operations.”

WindBorne CEO John Dean told TechCrunch in August that the company had raised a $37 million Series B round to continue scaling its business. Earlier this summer, the company released the latest version of its forecasting model, WeatherMesh 6, which it says provides more accurate forecasts than the traditional model run by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), which simulates the atmosphere using the laws of physics.

Since the arrival of transformer model architectures and the ECMWF’s release of a massive weather dataset a few years ago, AI weather forecasting has become one of the more productive uses of deep-learning technology. Meteorologists previously relied on expensive supercomputers running detailed equations that approximate how the atmosphere behaves. Now, end-to-end learning can ingest decades of weather data and issue predictions more quickly.

Models built by frontier labs and government agencies are proving more accurate than traditional forecasts, although it is still a jagged frontier, with both types of forecasts required to enable useful understanding of the weather. Google DeepMind’s latest weather model offers important new capabilities, and its cyclone forecasting tools are becoming increasingly central to how the US government responds to hurricane season.

In August WindBorne became the first organization to send an unpowered flight system — one with no engine — to collect data in the eye of a typhoon . The company maneuvers its balloons by adjusting their altitude, bleeding air, or dropping sand carried as ballast, to send the vehicles into winds that take them where they need to go.

“That’s a pretty novel step, and the two ingredients for that are one, having good wind and weather models, and knowing how to navigate them; and two, having a large enough constellation that you have balloons in the right places,” Sushko said. “It’s one of the first times that a deep-learning model was used for actual operational decisions.”

items.title: Muse Wonder Puts Meta Back at the AI Frontier
items.summary: Meta’s biggest model rivals the world’s best—and includes new features to keep agents from going off the rails.
items.content:
When Mark Zuckerberg rebooted his company’s artificial intelligence efforts last year, it seemed to be a very expensive gamble. Meta’s latest AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, seem to show that the bet is finally paying off by putting the company back at the frontier of AI development.

Muse Wonder Full boasts frontier capabilities, Meta says, meaning that it is among the most capable AI models in the world. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” the company said in a blog post today.

The Muse Wonder models will be available though an API and through Muse Code, a tool for writing software with AI. Meta says the best version of the model will power features across its platforms, including its Muse personal agent .

Zuckerberg overhauled his company’s AI research last year by sinking billions into the recently formed Meta Superintelligence Labs, and hiring the former Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang to lead it. This effort has sometimes been rocky , with some researchers not sticking around for long.

Meta was once a trailblazer in AI. Its Llama series of models were the first frontier open-weight offerings from a big lab. Llama, which could be downloaded and run on one’s own hardware, was widely adopted by researchers and startups.

But the company fell behind after delivering several disappointing versions of the model, and as Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google rapidly introduced more capable models.

Meta announced the first model from its new lab, Muse Spark , in April of this year. The company has also released a small open weight model called Muse Glimmer , and says it plans to release larger open-weight models in the future. It did not disclose details of how new Muse Wonder models were built or trained.

Muse Wonder was built to compete with the very best, however. Meta says the largest version of the new model outperforms Anthropic’s second-best model, Claude Fable 5.1, and ranks just below its best, Claude Opus 5.5, on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , a widely used aggregated score of model capabilities.

Meta says the model outperforms OpenAI’s best model, GPT-6 Astra, and both Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 on some specialized benchmarks, including ones that measure a model’s ability to work with legal documents and to build software. Benchmarks are not always a reliable measure of real-world performance, but this is still a significant step forward for Meta’s models.

Muse Wonder also includes two novel features designed to help make agents more effective and less inclined to misbehave. The new features, called Active Memory and Active Focus, are designed to keep the model locked into a stated goal, and prevent it from becoming confused. This can be a challenge when AI performs complex research or builds a large software project, for example, and can lead to expensive mistakes or compounded errors.

Meta says it has put significant effort into training Muse Wonder to refuse to generate dangerous outputs, such as recipes for building bioweapons or help with hacking. It says the company scores well on several benchmarks designed to measure how resilient models are to those prompts.

Zuckerberg said in a post on X last month that the company had delayed the release of its Muse models to work on safety. Meta also revealed a framework designed to ensure that it scales its models’ capabilities safely in a blog post earlier this month.

Muse Wonder may add more fuel to an already furious race to develop more capable AI, however. It certainly suggests that Meta is once again competitive in the increasingly high-stakes AI race.

items.title: Thinking will become a hobby
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.spinellis.gr/blog/20261008/?li261008 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50059204 Points: 210 # Comments: 275
items.content:
These lines are very difficult for me to write because I feel like digging my own grave. AI systems are improving by leaps and bounds. From the early 2022 fumbling release of ChatGPT, which couldn’t correctly count the number of a’s in my name (it claimed two), we reached OpenAI’s release of math papers where an internal AI model solved many hundreds of previously open math problems. Aside from philosophical arguments, practical claims regarding the superiority of human thought, on grounds such as hallucinations or bias, increasingly appear to me like rearguard defence. For the bulk of today’s cognitive work, the writing’s on the wall: AI will take over.

The three factors driving AI’s dominance in the modern work environment are better performance, lower cost, and higher availability. The performance of AI models is rising spectacularly on all fronts: perception, knowledge processing and creation, reasoning, judgement, and autonomous action. In parallel, human proficiency in key information-processing skills, low on average among adults , is even declining among students . Consequently, AI systems are performing better than humans in ever-wider range of tasks.

AI’s cost is also falling due to huge investments and scientific progress. Successive generations of AI models offer superior performance at lower cost, with older models retained only for backward compatibility. As a result, it is making financial sense to replace or augment human labour with AI systems across an increasingly broad range of activities.

Finally, and most obviously, AI systems can operate around the clock, without the need for rest or breaks. They can also help alleviate labour shortages arising from demographic trends or skills gaps. Meanwhile, trillions of dollars in projected data centre investment through 2030 are set to bring vast additional AI processing capacity online.

As happened in past technological revolutions, there will undoubtedly be fierce resistance to the replacement of cognitive work with AI. This time it will be fiercer because, unlike previous revolutions, which transformed manual labour, AI challenges knowledge workers, whose specialised expertise, control over information, and decision-making authority afford them greater economic and organisational power. Governments will try to clip AI’s wings through regulation and taxation. Such actions didn’t quell past revolutions so there’s little reason to believe they’ll work now.

So what’s the fate of human thought? My take is that cognitive work will diminish. Thought will increasingly become a leisure pursuit, as hunting did following animal domestication, calligraphy after typography, woodworking after industrialisation, and horse riding after motorisation. Machines transformed much of physical activity from necessity into choice; similarly, AI will decouple human thinking from its economic purpose.

I’ll end with my thoughts on how to prepare for and live through this transition. My take is that building this AI-driven world, riding through the bumps along the road, and preparing to live a fulfilling and satisfying life in an environment where AI dominates cognitive work will be hugely demanding, stressful, and intellectually challenging. Such is the nature of revolutions. Consequently, we must keep pace with and capitalise on AI’s advances; be flexible, adaptable, and resilient; and build a purposeful and rewarding life beyond work. My challenge ahead is to move from making a living by thinking, to making thinking part of a life worth living.

items.summary: Article URL: https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-wonder Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50059115 Points: 507 # Comments: 275
items.content:
A frontier model that leads on personal and professional agents

Today, we’re excited to introduce the Muse Wonder series with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, our most capable models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on personal and professional agentic tasks. Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence. Muse Wonder brings together Active Memory and Active Focus to keep track of what matters to you and work diligently toward what you want to accomplish.

Fourteen months ago, we began a ground-up overhaul of our artificial intelligence efforts. In that time, we’ve gone from rebuilding our stack from first principles to pushing the frontier.

When we introduced Muse Spark , we outlined our approach to predictable, rigorous scaling. Today’s release builds on that work across pretraining and reinforcement learning, delivering our most capable models yet. Trained at our gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full bring together the work of teams across Meta to deliver frontier capabilities for complex tasks at work and in everyday life — another step toward bringing personal superintelligence to the billions of people who use our products.

The Muse Wonder series achieves state-of-the-art results across key benchmarks for personal and professional agents, memory, and coding.

The full results below compare Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full with other frontier models across a broad evaluation suite.

For more details about our evaluations, see our report .

The results above provide a broad view of the models’ performance. We now take a closer look at four areas central to their work on real-world tasks: domain expertise, Active Memory, Active Focus, and frontier coding.

Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full apply specialized knowledge to problems people encounter at work and in daily life, from understanding a lease to making sense of financial or health information. Our evaluations include tasks in law, finance, and health that test this ability. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), for example, requires models to work with source documents and follow detailed instructions to produce legal work products.

One of the most critical steps towards useful personal and professional agents is reliable memory. Models need to remember what matters and recognize when earlier information becomes relevant. We call this Active Memory : carrying important context about you across conversations and actively retrieving the details relevant to the task at hand.

Using that context to complete a task also requires sustained effort. Active Focus describes how Muse Wonder continues working toward a challenging goal: trying alternative approaches, working through blockers, and adapting to new information. Along the way, it asks for clarification when needed and checks in before taking important actions. We evaluate focus through FocusBench and sustained execution through SWE-Marathon, which tests work on long-running software projects.

Coding brings these capabilities together. Building software requires tracking requirements, making changes across a codebase, and working through repeated cycles of testing and revision. Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full deliver frontier coding performance, supporting projects from small applications to complex software. We trained both models on diverse, long-running tasks to help them sustain progress across this process.

Muse Wonder builds a playable 3D kitchen game from customizable image inputs.

Two models often have similar benchmark scores, yet one seems to handle a much wider range of unfamiliar tasks. That’s what complaints of “benchmaxxing” and praise for “big model smell” both get at: a breadth of capability that popular benchmarks in a few domains can’t fully capture.

To quantify this mismatch, we investigate how performance on tasks targeted during post-training relates to performance on unfamiliar tasks as we scale test-time compute. The plot below compares Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder Full, with each point denoting performance at a distinct reasoning effort. The horizontal axis shows the model’s score on a composite representative of the tasks we focused on during post-training (“in-distribution”). The vertical axis shows the average score on a set of tasks we did not target during post-training (“out-of-distribution”).

Both of our models improve similarly on out-of-distribution tasks as we scale test-time compute. But given its in-distribution performance, Muse Wonder Full performs even better on unfamiliar tasks than the Muse Spark 1.3 trend would predict. This upward shift is because Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full build on larger, stronger base models: a stronger base yields post-training gains that carry over more effectively to unfamiliar tasks. That versatility especially matters for personal agents, which need to handle many combinations of goals, tools, and constraints — not all of which we can anticipate during training.

Working directly in a browser and across apps, Muse Wonder builds a running plan (Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors) based on personal preferences and circumstances.

Muse Wonder designs and orders custom swag based on real photos taken from a personal Instagram profile.

Muse Wonder prepares a custom wedding seating chart based on a list of complex matching requirements.

Delivering personal superintelligence to everyone requires a significant investment in alignment and safety. A personal agent takes actions on a user’s behalf and might handle context such as messages, calendars, and private documents. That level of access demands a model that exercises discretion with private information and resists misuse. We trained the Muse Wonder family to lead on both dimensions, with robustness to adversarial instructions and careful handling of private information.

items.title: A Modern Web App in C
items.summary: Article URL: https://prophitt.me/writing/a-modern-web-app-in-c Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50058528 Points: 362 # Comments: 157
items.content:
If you wanted a dynamic website in 1994, you wrote a C program, dropped it in a cgi-bin directory, and let Apache fork it per request. Thirty-two years later, I shipped a commercial web product using fundamentally the same technology.

Everything about marketyour.games is modern. It's a web product with user accounts, a search dashboard for content creators, folders for organizing them, payments via Stripe and transactional emails via Postmark. It follows progressive enhancement and doesn't require any JavaScript.

Everything is modern except the way it was made and how it is served. Here are my thoughts on writing a real product in C and serving it via CGI in 2026.

CGI's decline was justified in 2004 but doesn't hold up in 2026.

You can write a modern web application in C. I shipped one. One binary, a SQLite file, three dependencies and the entire thing fits in your head.

The stack is BCHS : OpenBSD, C, httpd, and SQLite.

There's no framework. You write a C program that reads CGI environment variables and responds.

There's no templating language. You write C that outputs the HTML directly.

There's no separate database server. You open the database file through SQLite's C API.

There's no container. You build a statically linked binary and drop it in a folder.

Every request spawns a fresh process. Deploying a new version is replacing one file. That means no server restart and no downtime. New requests simply pick up the new binary.

OpenBSD ships with sane defaults and gives you the tools to actually secure a C program like pledge and unveil. Httpd serves from a chroot by default, so your CGI binary runs sandboxed to its own corner of the filesystem.

I lean on three additional libraries:

libcurl handles all outbound requests to Stripe and Postmark.

libsodium handles random identifier generation, password hashing and the HMAC verification for Stripe webhooks.

libcjson handles JSON parsing for Stripe and Postmark.

Only two of those are actual build dependencies: libcurl and libsodium.

libcjson is a single C file and has no external dependencies. SQLite ships an official amalgamation (single C file) build.

Both are vendored and built as part of the project.

The result is a build with almost no moving parts. A clean build takes a few seconds and rebuilds complete in less than half a second.

Instead of serving static assets the traditional way, I route all traffic from httpd to the CGI binary. Every asset is compiled into the executable and served from memory.

Fundamentals over frameworks.

CGI isn't a framework to learn. The 1.1 specification was published in 2004 and hasn't changed since.

There's no API to internalize. The entire interface is a handful of fundamental HTTP concepts:

Request headers. Request methods. Query strings. Body data.

If you understand HTTP, you already understand CGI.

It's language and platform agnostic. You learn it once and the knowledge is good forever.

Clear separation of concerns.

A modern web application typically puts a web server like nginx in front and reverse-proxies to an application server written in another language like Ruby, Python, Go, or Rust. That always felt a bit strange to me: you essentially have two web servers, and one of them is also responsible for your business logic.

CGI gives you a single web server that calls your business logic directly. It's clear who does what.

It makes debugging simpler, too. Your application is an ordinary program you can run from a shell: pipe it a request, watch stderr, step through it with gdb.

In a sense, CGI resembles serverless architecture: a supervisor invokes your code per request, hands it a bag of environment variables, and collects the result. CGI is serverless, minus the vendor (and surprise bills).

Minimal supply chain risk.

With the rise of autonomous agents and weekly attacks on package repositories, it feels reassuring to have very few dependencies.

Most modern tech stacks come with a package manager and an ecosystem to go along with it. It's convenient, but the dependency graph balloons. One or two direct dependencies can pull in hundreds of indirect ones, each maintained by somebody you've never heard of, with publish credentials protected by a password reused since 2015.

My supply chain is a C compiler and three libraries. Compromising it would require compromising libcurl... a project the entire internet watches, not a package with eleven weekly downloads and an owner who left in 2019.

I'm a minimalist at heart. I use classic Vim with zero plugins. That means no LSP, no autocomplete, no code formatters, and no AI.

Complex tech stacks demand complex tooling: they demand a language server to wade through the layers of abstraction. But this stack is simple enough a plain editor is all you need. The entire application is a directory of C files and a Makefile.

Open a file, read it, and you know what it does.

Great tooling is within reach.

When you do want tooling, it's not far. Sanitizers, valgrind, gdb, ctags, cscope... these are mature (well, geriatric) tools that have been refined for decades and they're a package install away on any system that can compile C.

The maturity goes further than the tools themselves: integration is built into many editors. Vim ships with native support for ctags, cscope and has a graphical gdb frontend (see :h Termdebug).

Writing HTML and CSS in C isn't too bad.

I was hesitant to write the entire frontend in C, but it wasn't nearly as painful as I imagined.

All too many times have I:

Fought vim to highlight Go's html/template syntax. Fought helix to detect Go templates without breaking html detection. Fought rustrover to recognize jinja templates for a project using askama.

Using C means there's no second language for your editor to half-detect, no mixed-syntax where highlighting falls apart, no plugin dance to get the two languages to cooperate.

It was refreshing to just write C. It isn't pretty, but neither is Tailwind.

items.title: Honeyjar offers AI tools to improve PR and comms at every company
items.summary: Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?
items.content:
Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken (buy me a drink sometime, and I’ll give you my rant). But could AI actually make things better?

Honeyjar , which will be attending this week’s TechCrunch Disrupt as part of the Startup Battlefield 200 , wants to use AI to make the expertise and judgment of the best PR pros available to everyone, including founders who have no idea where to start.

The startup’s founders, CEO Michelle Masek and Chief Communications Officer Nadia Jamshidi, certainly fit the bill when it comes to PR expertise. They’ve both spent decades in the field, doing in-house communications and working at agencies. Masek recently served as senior vice president of marketing and communications for Ev Williams’ venture firm, Obvious Ventures .

As Masek described the challenges involved in “helping with the why and when of comms and marketing for 110 portfolio companies” (the startups her firm had invested in), I flashed back to my own brief stint leading marketing at an early-stage VC firm , where founders were constantly asking for help getting into TechCrunch. So I wasn’t surprised that Masek found herself asking, “Is there a way to scale the senior-level expertise into AI [in a way] that actually helps users do the work of comms in the proactive and skilled way that we do?”

Honeyjar is her answer to that question. It automates processes like writing announcements, finding the best journalists to pitch, and identifying the most promising speaking opportunities. But Jamshidi told me in a follow-up email that Honeyjar’s vision goes beyond getting press coverage and beyond specific AI tools.

“Honeyjar can find reporters, build media lists, scan news and social, track coverage, and surface opportunities,” she said. “Those capabilities are important, but they’re just one piece of what we’re building. The bigger idea is bringing the whole communications workflow together: signals, context, strategy, judgment, timing, and execution.”

And it’s not just for founders. Masek said she’s come to realize there are “millions and millions of unassigned communicators responsible for the work of comms.”

“They don’t have the title of comms, but they’re marketers, investors, authors, creators, school superintendents, sports team leaders,” she added. “It’s incredibly horizontal, this need to nail strategic communications. It’s always passed around, but the problems are very often not solved.”

Nor is Honeyjar trying to replace PR professionals. Masek said she and Jamshidi built the tool they wanted to use themselves. She argued that Honeyjar can make PR firms and in-house comms teams more effective, while allowing individual PR practitioners to “take on that third client without any scaling cost.”

When Honeyjar opened its waitlist, it received 10,000 signups in the first 24 hours, said Masek. Beta testers include Nextdoor, tech startup Coco Robotics, investor Bloomberg Beta, and agencies Mission North and Full Picture.

That sounds promising for companies looking to get more attention, but it could be a nightmare for journalists. We receive more pitches than we can respond to, many of them already written by AI chatbots.

When I raised my fears about getting inundated with even more PR slop, Masek noted that while Honeyjar can draft a pitch email or a social media post in the customer’s voice, the customer actually has to hit send or publish.

“We never want a world where the human is removed from the loop,” she said.

And that’s also where judgment is key. Masek said she and Jamshidi tried to “infuse and encode Honeyjar with our wisdom.” Through a broader initiative called the Comms Lab, they’re now training the product on the judgment of other PR pros as well.

“For us, judgment is knowing what to do, what not to do, when to act, and how to adapt to the situation,” Jamshidi added. “That comes from understanding a company’s goals and priorities, what’s happening inside and outside the organization, and knowing what to say, to whom, where, and when.”

In some cases, Masek said Honeyjar might even tell a founder that they’re simply not ready for coverage.

“We hear from reporters all the time who want better pitches, who want to hear from experts directly,” she said. “We actually see a future where there are more credible pitches in your inbox from sources who you actually want to hear from.”

items.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
items.summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.
items.content:
Microsoft president Brad Smith is calling for urgent regulation of AI, and his argument is that consumer products like milk and washing machines have more oversight than the companies building artificial intelligence.

On a recent BBC podcast , Smith called AI both a “weapon and a tool” that is putting the world’s cybersecurity at risk and said the “moment has arrived” to institute global safety rules.

Smith also said the U.K., and not the U.S. or European Union, is best placed to lead on global safety rules. Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI), launched in 2023, receives access to major models from U.S. frontier labs before they are deployed and has quickly become a leader in AI safety testing.

That role has been under threat in recent weeks, with U.S. president Donald Trump warning against “globalist” organizations, which he claims are interfering with American companies. Last month, he reportedly asked Anthropic and OpenAI to withhold new models from British testers, but AISI confirmed on Monday that it is able to access and test the latest models.

Despite the president’s pushback, however, Smith argued the U.K. can regulate AI in ways that the U.S. cannot.

“In Washington, D.C., people don’t look at the U.K. and they don’t look at London the way they look at Brussels,” he told the BBC. “That’s a strength.”

His comments come amid rallying cries from tech leaders, including Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman, to slow the pace of AI development in the wake of several incidents where AI agents went rogue.

Last month, Trump hosted tech leaders of companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, AMD, SpaceX, Meta, and Google, at the White House to discuss AI safety. They signed a “morally binding” document in which they agreed to work with “independent auditors” to assess the safety and capabilities of their AI models.

Smith says the document is a “good step,” but it stops short of the type of regulation that is necessary. The problem with voluntary self-regulation, he said, is that only the “good companies” will comply.

“It’s the companies that are not as responsible that you need to worry about,” he said.

Smith outlined several AI safety rules he’d like to see put into place, like a legal obligation to alert an organization if its system was breached by rogue AI agents. He also appears to be in favor of AI labs getting the approval of outside evaluators before an AI product is released and spoke positively about kill switches to pause or slow down AI if humans lose control of it.

“Let’s speak calmly, maybe even softly, but firmly, and start to bring people together,” Smith said. “I hope that’s the role we can play as a company. I hope that’s the role the U.K. can play as a country.”

items.title: This AI startup says it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes
items.summary: Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.
items.content:
Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Dram was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him.

There was just one problem: The technology his idea required didn’t exist yet.

“Then ChatGPT came along,” said Dram, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022.

His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF.

Blueprints AI , which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 , a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

During that 20-year lead-up to Blueprints AI, Dram earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in architecture from the University of Tehran and completed two years of PhD coursework on digital design at the European Graduate School in Switzerland. He moved to the United States and opened an architecture firm in 2018 called Drams Design-Build. Then, after obtaining a general contractor’s license, he added a construction business in 2021.

Dram should have been satisfied. He wasn’t.

“I was saying, okay, maybe I can build new projects that change people’s life in that area, but it wouldn’t be a big impact,” he said. “What makes me very excited about technology is the impact, the hours saved, the energy saved of people doing the same thing over and over and over.”

Blueprints AI will unveil a more capable second-generation version of its software at Disrupt. Dram and Cao say it will make a big impact because it takes over the repetitive drafting work that fills most of an architect’s day.

“It will make better spaces for people because now architects have the time to design,” said Dram. He said architects spend about 80% of their time on drafting and only 20% on design. “I want to flip that to be 20-80.”

Dram and Cao met at an AI conference several years ago and combined their skills to build the company. Cao, a data scientist from Hong Kong, handles sales and go-to-market strategy as chief commercial officer.

The pair trained their models using eight years of approved drawing sets from Dram’s design and construction firm, which is still in business.

Its first-generation software produces architectural construction documents and costs between $3,200 and $8,500 a month, depending on the plan. Custom pricing for enterprises is also available.

The startup’s second-generation software will deliver a considerable upgrade. Customers can start with a description or sketch of a project and create blueprints for every aspect of a building at once, including architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and interior design. Version 2 allows users to design and make changes to the project, an upgrade over the first iteration. Importantly, one design change updates the entire project and is checked against local building codes.

Early customers are already using the second version, and Dram said it will become publicly available this week. The startup is already working on a third version of its software that will add in structural analysis and electrical panel design.

The technology doesn’t replace licensed architects, according to the co-founders. Licensed professionals still review the documents and affix their seal before submitting them for permits. The judgment stays human, they say.

Blueprints AI is targeting two groups with its new software. Professional architecture, engineering, and design firms make up one group, while developers and real estate owners make up another. The startup offers its software as a subscription and may add a one-time flat-fee option for those who just want it for a single project.

To learn more about Blueprints, catch hundreds of other startups, and learn from headliners like RJ Scaringe of Rivian and Amjad Masad of Replit, join us at TechCrunch Disrupt , kicking off Tuesday in downtown San Francisco.

items.title: Fitbit Edge is Google’s middle ground between Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch
items.summary: Google’s newest wearable costs $179.99 and has a sleek feel like the Fitbit Air but with an OLED display.
items.content:
Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch.

Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls.

It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)

Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.

The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.

Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters.

The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27.

Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99.
